notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — three P1 findings concentrate on API-shape decisions that are difficult to reverse post-publication (at_type doc/code/PLAN drift, JsContactId inconsistency) and one P2 spec-divergence (u32 vs UnsignedInt) that has near-zero practical trigger today but is documented nowhere.
Confidence: ~85% chance of no missed correctness bug. Least confident flag: JMAP-sgrr.6 (the serde flatten + rename interaction for @type is reasoned-from-docs not verified by test or probe — it could in principle fail in a serde minor release without the existing tests catching it). Uncertainty driven by: (a) no test fixture exercises @type on the wire, so the read-only review cannot empirically confirm flatten priorities; (b) the manual AnniversaryDate Deserialize at lib.rs:977-997 has one edge case (non-object Unknown round-trip, JMAP-sgrr.9) that I am 95% sure is a real asymmetry but I did not write a probe. Would raise confidence if: a probe is written under /do-beads JMAP-sgrr.6 to confirm @type round-trip, and another under JMAP-sgrr.9 to demonstrate the non-object asymmetry. Both probes are forbidden in this read-only review pass.
API contract risk: MEDIUM — typed sub-types are sound for round-trip and have good non_exhaustive coverage, but the partial-response Option model pushes many invariants into runtime caller checks (mandatory-as-Option for 8 fields, pref/list_as/month/day with no range bound, contexts as HashMap<String,bool> permitting false, JsContactId without validation helper or Display). serde_json re-exports across Unknown variant and 28 extras fields are an undocumented version-pin contract.
API contract confidence: 75% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-sgrr.18 (HashMap<String,bool> set-as-map — fix is breaking and the convention is used across the whole workspace, including jmap-jscalendar-types; this is closer to 'all of the workspace contexts fields' than a single-crate issue); JMAP-sgrr.21 (Resource trait — debatable whether the abstraction earns its keep; PLAN.md explicitly considered and rejected it). Uncertainty driven by: cannot run cargo test or cargo doc to verify the README doctest at README.md:65-78 compiles, and cannot probe the @type-into-extras serde-flatten interaction empirically (which JMAP-sgrr.6 already calls out as a probe-required gap).
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — code reads as idiomatic Rust modulo two findings this pass (sgrr.26 string-sentinel in AnniversaryDate::deserialize, sgrr.27 #[non_exhaustive] constructor gap). No unsafe, no gratuitous clones, no Box<dyn Error>, no exported macros, no production .unwrap() / .expect(), no clippy::* anti-patterns in the diff. Manual Serialize/Deserialize for AnniversaryDate is justified by the #[serde(untagged)] mis-dispatch risk (every PartialDate field is Option so untagged would swallow a Timestamp). The clone() usages are all in test code. The remaining idiom gaps that overlap with the my-oss findings (.13 JsContactId Display/FromStr, .7 missing Eq derives, .21 Resource trait absence, .25 redundant #[non_exhaustive] on private-field newtype, .19 serde_json::Value in public enum variant) are already filed under non-idiom labels and not re-filed here per the prompt's no-duplicate rule.
Rust idiom confidence: ~10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: sgrr.27 (constructor gap is workspace-wide and PLAN.md does not say whether external-crate construction is in-scope for the kit's public API contract — could be a deliberate 'use serde' decision rather than an oversight; if so, this is taste not idiom). sgrr.26 is high-confidence (the unwrap_or("") + "" arm is unambiguously the sentinel anti-pattern). Uncertainty driven by: (a) cannot run cargo clippy in read-only mode to confirm no warning is being silently suppressed; (b) cannot probe whether a Default impl for Relation / Author / Pronouns / SpeakToAs would conflict with workspace constructor-policy not stated in PLAN.md or workspace AGENTS.md. Two findings is on the low end and the workspace AGENTS.md anti-bikeshedding warning applies here — I deliberately did not flag: builder-pattern absence (workspace policy not stated), HashMap vs BTreeMap for sort_as (serde_json sorts keys on output, no observable difference), #[serde(transparent)] vs implicit-transparent newtype divergence from jscalendar-types (zero functional impact), and the From<&str> vs FromStr choice for JsContactId (already covered by .13 / .23). If a future contributor disagrees with sgrr.27 on policy grounds, closing it as not-a-bug is fine; the finding documents the trade-off.
API contract risk (supplement pass): MEDIUM — three new findings on the AnniversaryDate/Timestamp dispatch boundary (sgrr.28 + sgrr.29 at P2: silent round-trip variant identity loss in two opposite directions) and the cross-field-constraints pattern across 6 structs (sgrr.30 at P3, doc-only mitigation). Supplement pass does not change the overall risk class from the prior /review-myoss verdict; it adds three footguns that the my-oss pass missed because they sit at the AnniversaryDate dispatch boundary rather than in per-struct field shapes.
API contract supplement confidence: ~80% chance of no missed api-contract issue. Least confident flags: sgrr.28 (the AnniversaryDate::Unknown round-trip asymmetry could be argued as deliberate scope — the doc promises fidelity for 'future-spec @type variant' specifically, which technically excludes wrapping known-shape Values; a future contributor disagreeing on the scope of the round-trip contract is plausible and the finding could be closed not-a-bug on that ground). sgrr.29 is high-confidence (the dispatch trace is unambiguous and the test for at_type=None Timestamp is genuinely missing). sgrr.30 is low-stakes (it's a docs aggregation finding, the constraints are already documented per-struct). Uncertainty driven by: (a) cannot run cargo test to verify the two probe assertions in sgrr.28 and sgrr.29 empirically; (b) deliberately did not refile under api-contract labels the prior pass's findings that are substantively the same complaint (sgrr.13, .14, .15, .17, .18, .22, .23, .25, .27) — those would be bikeshedding by relabeling. If the convention for /review-library-supplement is to mirror api-contract labels onto existing my-oss-labeled findings rather than file only new ones, this pass under-files by ~9 findings.
Idiom rating (re-pass 2026-05-14): ACCEPTABLE — confirms prior pass. No new findings filed. The two existing idiom-specific findings (sgrr.26 string-sentinel anti-pattern, closed; sgrr.27 constructor gap, open) plus the idiom-adjacent findings already covered under other labels (sgrr.13 Display/FromStr, sgrr.7 Eq derives, sgrr.21 Resource trait, sgrr.25 redundant non_exhaustive, sgrr.19 serde_json in public variant) remain the complete set. The crate has no unsafe, no production unwrap/expect, no Box<dyn Error>, no gratuitous clones, no exported macros, no lifetime annotations, no for-loop accumulation, no bool parameters in disguise, no Option<bool> in public API, no clippy::* anti-patterns. The single manual Serialize/Deserialize impl (AnniversaryDate, lib.rs:1034-1077) is justified by the doc rationale and reads as idiomatic Rust (Option<&str> match arm, .and_then(.as_str), is_object() short-circuit before object dispatch). Test helpers use .unwrap() per test idiom; this is not a flag.
Rust idiom confidence (re-pass): ~5% chance of missed issue. Least confident: the bikeshedding boundary on JsContactId — its Display/FromStr/Borrow story differs from foundation jmap-types::Id (which has Borrow<str>, PartialEq<str>, into_inner via macro) but matches sibling jmap-jscalendar-types newtypes (AsRef<str> only). Workspace has no canonical-template rule for scalar newtypes specifically, so consistency direction is ambiguous; sgrr.13 covers the gap as a separate finding. Uncertainty driven by: (a) cannot run cargo clippy in read-only mode to confirm no auto-fix lint suppressed; (b) the prior pass's confidence was already at 10% — re-running cannot meaningfully lower it without an empirical signal a probe would provide. Anti-bikeshedding warning from workspace AGENTS.md is in force: filing additional findings would be padding, not signal.
